figures.finding: China's National Film Industry Development Special Fund is a government fund fed by 5% of every commercial cinema's box-office revenue (the 2015 Measures, in force from 1 October 2015) and used, among other things, to reward the production, distribution and screening of outstanding domestic films; it had a 2.3 billion yuan annual budget by 2017 and rewards selected films with prizes of up to 6 million yuan each (20 of 30 short-listed titles, each with over 100,000 admissions and 20 million yuan at the box office).

value.fund: National Film Industry Development Special Fund

figures.applies: China; as Sixth Tone reported in July 2017.

sources.said: 第三条 电影专项资金属于政府性基金，全额上缴中央和地方国库，纳入中央和地方政府性基金预算管理。 … 第七条 办理工商注册登记的经营性电影放映单位，应当按其电影票房收入的5%缴纳电影专项资金。 … （四）奖励优秀国产影片制作、发行和放映。 … 第二十七条 本办法自2015年10月1日起施行。

The film fund was established in 1996 to help develop China’s domestic film industry … its annual budget is 2.3 billion yuan . All Chinese movie theaters must give 5 percent of their revenue — including revenue generated from foreign films — to the film fund’s provincial offices … It must also have been viewed by over 100,000 people in cinemas and have made at least 20 million yuan at the box office. Out of the 30 films that make the short list, 20 are selected by a committee of officials and industry representatives to receive prizes of up to 6 million yuan each.
